item.title: Forecasters sound the alarm over a powerful El Nino climate pattern
item.description: Forecasters expect the El Niño weather pattern to strengthen significantly this year, raising the risks of extreme weather around the world well into 2027.
item.content:encoded: Forecasters expect the El Niño weather pattern to strengthen significantly this year, raising the risks of extreme weather around the world well into 2027.

item.title: Inside the failed mission to eliminate FEMA
item.description: David Richardson worked to eliminate the country's top disaster agency when he led FEMA last year. Now, he says the administration has abandoned that goal.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: U.N. climate report warns world will soon cross a dangerous threshold
item.description: A new United Nations report finds that the world will soon pass a dangerous threshold for climate warming. Countries had agreed to limit warming to that level to avoid the most extreme impacts.
item.content:encoded: A new United Nations report finds that the world will soon pass a dangerous threshold for climate warming. Countries had agreed to limit warming to that level to avoid the most extreme impacts.

item.title: Chevron's expansion in Venezuela has implications for the oil industry and the planet
item.description: Chevron is expanding its current operations in Venezuela. The deal expands the company's footprint at a time of political and economic uncertainty in Venezuela.

item.description: Chevron is the largest foreign oil operator in Venezuela. The deal will expand its footprint at a time of political and economic uncertainty for Venezuela.

item.title: He died of 'natural causes.' But his mother says she knows what killed him: heat
item.description: When Arizona counts heat-related deaths, Adam Willson isn't included. His story shows how thousands of heat deaths can go uncounted every year in the United States.

item.title: The U.S.-Venezuela oil deal won't lower your gas prices. Here's what you need to know
item.description: The Trump administration announced a deal Friday to develop a vast amount of Venezuela's oil reserves, with the U.S. taking a majority stake. Energy experts say there are many reasons to be skeptical.

item.title: NPR spent 2 years tracking deaths from heat. We found a staggering hidden toll
item.description: An NPR investigation found that people in the U.S. are dying from heat much more often than official counts show. We explore the reasons why — and how lives can be saved.

item.title: Arizona's taps won't run dry, but water bills will go up under federal plan for Colorado River
item.description: New federal rules mean Arizona will be getting a lot less water from the Colorado river. City leaders say they've been planning for years and no one will run out, but keeping taps flowing is expensive.
